/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 16 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3327 (-33)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5612 (-75)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2325 (-39)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1748 (12)
Baltic Handysize Index: 961 (13)
CAPESIZE
The market softened further today, with weakness in the Pacific outweighing improving sentiment in the Atlantic basin. While the South Atlantic remained resilient and showed signs of strengthening on the back of increased activity, a lack of volume in the Pacific continued to pressure rates. The BCI 182 5TC declined by $675 on the day to close at $50,900. The C5 index fell by $0.414 to $16.041, while the C3 index gained $0.691 to settle at $42.559. In the Pacific, sentiment remained under pressure as limited activity and a growing tonnage list weighed on the market. With only one miner active on C5, trading was relatively subdued. Rio entered the market bidding $15.50 at the start of the day against offers in the low $16s, with fixtures ultimately concluded at $16.00 and $15.95. The South Atlantic, meanwhile, remained resilient and showed further signs of improvement, with rates strengthening throughout the day. $42.30 was paid for mid-October dates, before $42.60 was concluded for 15-20 October loading. Offers were subsequently withdrawn, with brokers indicating levels at or above $43.00, although for index dates there was still a sense that rates would trade at a slight discount.
PANAMAX
Published index routes weakened today, with the P5TC declining by $349 to settle at $20,927, reflecting softer sentiment across the markets despite pockets of improving activity. Market sources reported a pickup in activity on the trans-Atlantic route, with tonnage from the North Continent said to be attracting particular interest. Despite the increase in enquiry, overall sentiment remains subdued. Brokers noted that Owners have adjusted their offers downward, bringing them closer to bid levels and helping to narrow the rate spreads seen earlier in the week. The fronthaul market has also shown signs of increased activity. However, the available tonnage list has expanded as some Owners, who had previously dismissed fronthaul opportunities in favour of remaining within the Atlantic basin, are now reconsidering their positioning and becoming more open to these cargoes. In the Pacific, market participants reported another active day, however, an expanding tonnage list continued to weigh on underlying fundamentals. As a result, the increased activity was insufficient to prevent a decline in confirmed fixture rates, which remained under pressure throughout the session. Mineral demand from India has been in the spotlight with multiple reported fixtures from both Indonesia and Australia.
SUPRAMAX
Another positive day with the East leading the way, with both the North Pacific and South East Asia both showing gains, especially for trips Indonesia to India. The 11TC average was up $156 today to settle at $22,097. The Atlantic was more subdued with the main mover being the fronthaul from the Mediterranean.

Atlantic
Wooyang were rumoured to have taken an Ultramax on subjects to cover their Mississippi River grains to Vietnam for 1-10 October at $33,000 and the Magellan Eternity (63,611 2023) Tampa 24 September went on subjects delivery New Orleans for a trip Mediterranean with grains at the same level with Bunge. The SSI Invictus (63,735 2024) New Orleans end September was said to be on subjects with Cargill for grains to ARAG in the low $30,000’s (basis scrubber benefit for Charterers) and XO apparently fixed the LMZ Europa (56,771 2011) Puerto Cortez 20 September on subjects basis delivery NC South America for a trip Baltic with coal at $25,000. Cosco booked a Bulk Trading petcoke stem 55,000/10 Houston to Rizhao at $66.50 fio basis 15,000shinc load/10,000shinc discharge and Arcelormittal were said to be on subjects for 50,000/10 coal Mobile to Praia Mole 25 September/3 October at something in the $23’s basis 25,000shinc load/20,000shinc discharge. Arcelormittal were also linked with the Sakura L (63,742 2018) open Sandy Hook 26-27 September on subjects for legs, but no further details emerged, and the Avra (61,225 2020) Fairless Hills 23 September was reportedly on subjects to Norden for a trip Continent with woodpellets, but no rate was mentioned.

Asia
The Ocean Prosper (56,032 2013) prompt Kwangyang went on subjects to Samjoo for a trip via Gulf of Aden to the Mediterranean (basis no deck/hatchcover cargo) at $24,000 and the Jia Yue (63,319 2019) Cebu prompt was also rumoured to be on subjects for the same route/redelivery at $23,000, although sources questioned this level which was expected to be higher. The Yasa Mars (61,081 2019) Chittagong 18 September was placed on subjects for a trip via Indonesia to WC India at $22,000 and the Common Luck (58,799 2012) reportedly fixed delivery Saldanha Bay for a trip Japan at $23,000 plus $230,000 ballast bonus.
HANDYSIZE
The Handysize market delivered a mixed performance, with sentiment largely shaped by positional dynamics. The Continent and Mediterranean remained relatively firm, supported mainly by scrap business. The Eco Tide (35,914 2011) was placed on subjects for a trip via ARAG to the East Mediterranean with scrap at $25,000 by Pangea, while the Vantage Geilo (33,393 2015) was also placed on subjects for a trip via Aalborg to the East Mediterranean with scrap at $29,000 by Lauritzen, although further details were not confirmed. Meanwhile, the South Atlantic maintained its upward momentum, with participants remaining optimistic as rates strengthened further. The US Gulf continued to perform strongly following several firm fixtures for trips into the Mediterranean. The Lan Bao Hai (39,779 2015) was placed on subjects for a trip from the Mississippi River to Turkey with grains at $28,000 by Bunge, while the Paris Trader (40,292 2023) was reported fixed from Atlantic Colombia to Nador with coal in the mid-$20,000s by Centurion, although further details were not disclosed. In contrast, the Pacific market remained largely stagnant, with fundamentals little changed, limited fresh enquiry reported, and sentiment broadly flat across the region. Reflecting these regional variations, the 7TC average rose by $246 to close at $17,305.
